### Country-specific policy context

<div class="country-policy-context">In practice, PQ14 is provided without G6PD testing with counselling emphasized and heightened pharmacovigilance. Advise patient to look out for the signs of hemolysis. All patients with 14 days prescribed Primaquine (PQ) must be advised that if their urine becomes dark (reddish brown), they must stop taking PQ and return to the clinic as soon as possible.<br>Ongoing guidelines update will include use of the STANDARD test which will guide whether patients can receive 7-day high dose PQ (1mg/kg/day). This will be the main recommendation; however, if G6PD testing is not possible the current plan is to have the 14-day low dose PQ as a fall back. For the G6PDd individuals thinking of using 8-week PQ but ongoing discussion with PNG-IMR. Referral to rural health clinic from nurse aid - reviewed on day 3. There are ongoing challenges with limited supplies for G6PD reagents and RDTs. Adherence to the 14-day regimen is also a main issue.</div>
